# iliad-110 — review, pass 1 (Iliad 17.198–287)

Scope: grammatical labels in the notes, Greek to `l` word by word, `l` against `i`, remembered English, quotation marks, hand scan of flagged lines, cross-references, and the drafter's worries. `t` was not touched (checked: all 64 `t` values are byte-identical to before). Edits made by script to `units.json` in place. Gloss check (pass 2) not yet done.

Severity: major = the build or validator would refuse it; moderate = contradicts a binding house rendering or a parse; minor = fidelity or polish.

## Hand scan of 259
Μηριόνης ἀτάλαντος Ἐνυαλίῳ ἀνδρειφόντῃ: Μη-ρι-ο | νης ἀ-τά | λαν-τος Ἐ | νυ-α-λίῳ | ἀν-δρει | φόν-τῃ. Feet 1–3 are dactyls; foot 4 is a dactyl only if -ιῳ is read as one syllable (synizesis); foot 5 (ἀν-δρει) is a spondee. So the irregularity is real (spondaic fifth, with synizesis), and the sc already in iliad-013 (651), -042, -048 agrees. No other line in the part is flagged.

## Cross-references checked (all true)
2.484–492 (appeal to the Muses; 493 begins the ships, so the range is right); 2.674 (τῶν ἄλλων Δαναῶν μετ’ ἀμύμονα Πηλεΐωνα, Nireus; the same line is the last of the published iliad-013 unit at 671–674); 2.858 (Ennomus οἰωνιστής); 2.79 (= 248, Nestor); 2.166 (ὣς ἔφατ’, οὐδ’ ἀπίθησε); 1.528 (209) and 1.530 (ἐλέλιξεν “shook”, Olympus); 4.253 (συῒ εἴκελος ἀλκήν); 11.293 (ἀγροτέρῳ συῒ καπρίῳ); 14.216 (ὀαριστύς); 16.66 (κυάνεον Τρώων νέφος). Internal: 222 ↔ 261 (ἤγειρα / ἤγειραν), 227 ↔ 273 (τώ), 255 ↔ 272 (Τρῳῇσι/Τρῳῇσιν), 235 (Telamon’s Ajax), 284 (greater Ajax named), “the speech runs to 232”, ὅσσον in 242, simile 263–265 with τόσσῃ at 266. Speech marks: four speeches (Zeus 201–208, Hector 220–232, Ajax 238–245, Menelaus 248–255), each “ on the `mark` unit and ” on its last; 4/4 in `l` and in `i`; none runs on from or into a neighbouring part. Paragraph flags `p` match the ¶ lines (198, 209, 233, 246, 256, 262, 274).

## Findings considered and refused
- 205 οὐ κατὰ κόσμον: `l` “not in due order” is the table’s; `i` “not as was fitting” departs from the table’s 8.12 “in no good order” but that row is of a different context (struck down), the departure is recorded in new-renderings.md and the note explains it. Kept.
- 243–244 (νέφος … Ἕκτωρ): the note’s reading (Ἕκτωρ in apposition to the cloud; 16.66 for the cloud) is one of the two possible constructions (Hector as subject of καλύπτει with νέφος as object is the other); it does not change `l` or `i` materially and the note is hedged enough for a reader. The English “the cloud of war” supplies a definite article the Greek lacks; kept, because the cloud is identified with Hector in the next word.
- 228 ἣ: printed ἣ, so the pronoun “this” (not ἦ “truly”); note and `l` agree. Kept.
- 277–278: καὶ τοῦ (genitive of separation, “even from it”), μέλλον with the future infinitive ἀπέσσεσθαι (of ἄπειμι), μίνυνθα with the whole clause: parse correct; only the table wording of μίνυνθα changed (above).
- 285 μετεισάμενος: the note’s hedge (“aorist middle participle of the verb behind ἐείσατο”) is true and does not overclaim; `l`/`i` “rushing in among them” fits μετά + the verb. Kept.
- 207 ὅ τοι … ἐκνοστήσαντι: ὅ as “because/that” (neuter conjunction), τοι “from you” agreeing with the participle, is the usual construction; note says “neuter ‘that, in that’, not the relative ὅς”, which is true enough. Kept.
- 281–282 “a wild boar” in `i` for συῒ … καπρίῳ: “wild” is not a separate word here (unlike 11.293), but κάπριος is the wild boar and the two nouns are collapsed in `i` as at 11.293. Kept. (`l` “swine … a boar” also kept.)
- 234 “their hearts hoped” (`i`) for singular θυμός: English plural over a plural possessor; kept. 238 “even we two ourselves”: stiff but grammatical; kept.
- 236 `l` ends “foolish ones!” where t has ano teleia: punctuation is the drafter’s call and does not change sense. Kept.
- Previously published lines inside units (248, 259, 262, 280): their `l` wording is reused as far as the sentence allows; no change needed.

## units.json change from pass 2
- 284 (unit note): “βέβασαν is a perfect, ‘have taken their stand’ (Attic βεβήκασι)” was wrong, and the glossary entry (pluperfect, unaugmented) is right: the clause is in past narrative beside φρόνεον, and `l` already says “had taken their stand”. Note now says “an unaugmented pluperfect, ‘had taken their stand’ (Attic ἐβεβήκεσαν)”. (Moderate; it was a pass-1 miss.)

## Checked and left
- βέβασαν, ἀποδάσσομαι (ἀποδατέομαι, fut. mid., epic -σσ-), μίσησεν (aor. of μισέω + acc. + inf.): parses correct.
- Proper names (Μέσθλης, Μέδων, Θερσίλοχος, Δεισήνωρ, Ἀστεροπαῖος, Ἱππόθοος, Φόρκυς, Ἔννομος not novel, Μενοιτιάδην): forms and cases correct.
- κορέει (known: future 3 sg., “will sate”), κράτος (known: “strength, power, might”, object use covered), φάλαγγας (known: battle-line), αἰζηοὺς (known: vigorous young man), Μενοιτιάδῃ (known): the known entries cover the uses here and agree with the pass-1 renderings; no broadening needed.
- ἐνυάλιος, ὀαριστύς: gloss mentions “of close fighting”, a general sense of the word as used of war, not a line pin; left.
- Limit of this check: the 379 known-form entries were checked for the forms the part uses in a non-ordinary way (list above plus the particles and prepositions); a full read of every general entry for coverage was not made.

## new-renderings.md
Rewritten to match the final units and the table: dropped rows that follow the table or published parts (ἆ δείλ’, καταθύμιος, νήπιοι, νεμεσιζέσθω, ὀαριστύς), updated ἐλελίζω (`l` “whirled round”, after 5.497), tightened οὐ κατὰ κόσμον and συῒ … καπρίῳ, kept ἀπάνευθεν, ἕλον, δήμια πίνουσιν; added a one-paragraph list of table-following renderings so nothing is lost.
